Issues.Title: Fix Issue 15162: [Dark Mode] The dotnet line of button is black in DarkMode
Issues.Body: Fixes #15162 ## Root Cause This regression was most likely introduced by PR #13608. In the button rendering of DarkMode, the focus frame is changed to the ControlPaint.DrawFocusRectangle(...) path; under this color combination of .NET 11, black pixels will appear in the focus point line, resulting in a "black dot line" in the visual sense. ## Proposed changes - Added a shared `DrawDottedFocusRectangle(...)` method to `ButtonDarkModeRendererBase` that draws the focus rectangle using a specific dotted pen (eliminating reliance on the color-blending results of `ControlPaint.DrawFocusRectangle`). - Updated both `FlatButtonDarkModeRenderer` and `PopupButtonDarkModeRenderer` to use this shared method for rendering the focus indicator. - Added a regression test, `FlatButtonDarkModeRenderer_FocusIndicator_DoesNotPaintBlackPixels`, to ensure the dotted focus line no longer produces black pixels. ## Customer Impact - In Dark Mode, the focus indicator becomes clearly visible (a bright dashed line) when a button is focused via the Tab key, improving readability and accessibility; the change is limited to the rendering layer, with no changes to the public API. ## Regression? - Yes ## Risk - Mini ## Screenshots ### Before ### After ## Test methodology - Manual ## Test environment(s) - 11.0.100-rc.1.26420.103 ###### Microsoft Reviewers: [Open in CodeFlow](https://microsoft.github.io/open-pr/?codeflow=https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/pull/15196)

Issues.Title: Fix Issue 15190: TreeNodeCollection indexer setter throws NullReferenceException for a TreeNode not attached to a TreeView (regression since .NET 6)
Issues.Body: Fixes #15190 ## Root Cause This regression appears to have been introduced by https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/pull/4297. Following changes in .NET 6, the indexer setter (`this[int index]`) for `TreeNodeCollection` introduced logic to prevent duplicate nodes; however, it assumes the owner is already bound to a `TreeView` and directly accesses `_owner._treeView!`. When the owner is a detached `TreeNode` (not yet attached to any `TreeView`), `_owner._treeView` is `null`, triggering a `NullReferenceException` during subsequent access to `tv.Handle` or `tv._nodesByHandle`. ## Proposed changes - Change the resolution of the setter's owner to a nullable-safe flow (using `TreeView? tv = _owner.TreeView`), handling both the detached and attached scenarios. - For detached paths: Retain the legacy "managed-only" replacement semantics (to avoid NREs and support reordering via swap/sort); and add `_owner.CheckParentingCycle(value)` to prevent circular references. - For the `attached` path: Retain existing cross-TreeView and duplicate-node protections; continue using the `Remove(actual)` + `Insert(index, value)` approach to ensure consistency in states such as handles, the node table, tooltips, and accessibility. ## Customer Impact - Fixed a regression affecting .NET 6+: Swapping nodes via the indexer on a detached `TreeNodeCollection` for sorting purposes no longer throws a `NullReferenceException`. - Restored behavior consistent with earlier versions (allowing nodes to be reordered while detached before being attached to a `TreeView`). ## Regression? - Yes ## Risk - Mini ## Screenshots ### Before ### After ## Test methodology - Automation - Manual ## Test environment(s) - 11.0.100-rc.1.26420.103 ###### Microsoft Reviewers: [Open in CodeFlow](https://microsoft.github.io/open-pr/?codeflow=https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/pull/15195)

Issues.Title: release-notes in .NET 11 RC2
Issues.Body:
## Overall summary

- **Total qualifying PRs:** 16 merged PRs in milestone `11.0-rc2`.
- **Main feature areas:** WinForms design-time analyzers; Visual-style compatibility; Designer property serialization; Net11 rendering, layout, DPI, and right-to-left behavior; 
- **Key fixes worth highlighting:** 
    - New Designer guardrail analyzers
    - Introduces a per-state border stroke model for Net11 editable controls
    - The WPF Clipboard exception compatibility switch
    - Temporary Classic rendering defaults and opt-in switches for ToolStrip and DataGridView
    - Broad TextBox, ComboBox, and UpDown sizing corrections
    - Fixes for GroupBox images, explicit colors, RTL layouts, and DataGridView-hosted controls.

## New feature: design-time analyzers

| PR | Fixed Contents | Description | Comment |
|---|---|---|---|
| [#15148](https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/pull/15148) | `System.Windows.Forms.Analyzers` | Adds C# and Visual Basic Designer guardrails for invalid designer partial structures, unsupported or unrolled `InitializeComponent` code, CodeDOM-incompatible constructs, VB `WithEvents`/`Handles` wiring, and property getters that allocate new instances. It also adds the shared analyzer test infrastructure and diagnostic documentation. | **Include.** This is a substantial, enabled-by-default developer feature that can prevent Designer loading and serialization failures and can introduce new build diagnostics. |

## Compatibility and behavioral configuration

| PR | Fixed Contents | Description | Comment |
|---|---|---|---|
| [#15035](https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/pull/15035) | `System.Windows.Clipboard`; `Windows.Clipboard.ThrowExceptionsForGetAPIs` | Adds an opt-in AppContext switch that restores the pre-.NET 10 behavior of propagating failures from WPF Clipboard `Get*` APIs instead of returning empty data. The switch is applied to shared OLE object, HGLOBAL, IStream, and bitmap retrieval paths. | **Include.** Existing WPF applications may rely on exceptions to detect Clipboard failures, so the named compatibility switch must be discoverable. |
| [#15033](https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/pull/15033) | `Control.VisualStylesMode`; `ToolStrip`; `MenuStrip`; `DataGridView` | Makes composite controls use Classic rendering when Net11 styling is requested, avoiding clipping, row-height, padding, border, and hosted-editor regressions. Applications can opt back into modern rendering with `System.Windows.Forms.ToolStripModernRendering` and `System.Windows.Forms.DataGridViewModernRendering`. | **Include.** This changes the default rendering of major controls and introduces two user-configurable switches that adopters of Net11 visual styles need to understand. |

## Designer and property behavior

| PR | Fixed Contents | Description | Comment |
|---|---|---|---|
| [#15019](https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/pull/15019) | `System.Windows.Forms.Control.VisualStylesMode` | Fixes setting `VisualStylesMode` to `Classic` in the Properties window. The setter now clears the local value only when `Inherit` is explicitly assigned, so `Classic` no longer immediately reverts to `Inherit` or disappears from generated Designer code. | **Include.** This is a visible Designer serialization fix for a new .NET 11 property and preserves explicit values when the parent mode changes. |

## Visual rendering, layout, DPI, and RTL

| PR | Fixed Contents | Description | Comment |
|---|---|---|---|
| [#15147](https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/pull/15147) |  `TextBoxBase`; `TextBox`; `MaskedTextBox`; `RichTextBox `|  Adds a per-state border stroke model for Net11 editable controls, with distinct Rest, Hover, Focused, Disabled, and ReadOnly states. It also adds a stronger bottom elevation edge and an accent-colored bottom edge for the focused state, with border colors independent of ForeColor. | **Include.** This introduces a user-visible visual improvement to common editable controls under VisualStylesMode.Net11, including new state-specific border and focus rendering. |
| [#15159](https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/pull/15159) | `CheckBox`; `RadioButton`; `GroupBox.BackgroundImage` | Corrects Net11 background compositing so CheckBox and RadioButton controls with opaque effective backgrounds fill with `BackColor`, while transparent or translucent controls still composite the parent. This prevents a GroupBox background image from incorrectly showing through opaque controls. | **Include.** It fixes a prominent Net11 rendering defect while preserving intentional transparency. |
| [#14929](https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/pull/14929) | Net11 `Button`, `CheckBox`, and `RadioButton` color inheritance | Replaces incorrect serialization-based color tests with effective inheritance logic. Modern renderers now retain inherited non-default foreground colors and treat backgrounds as custom only when explicitly set. | **Include.** It prevents color regressions in customized containers and applications adopting Net11 styling. |
| [#14910](https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/pull/14910) | `System.Windows.Forms.GroupBox.BackgroundImage` | Draws one continuous client-coordinate background image across GroupBox header and body regions for Standard, Flat, and Popup styles. It also applies the intended overlays and prevents image leakage into child backgrounds and rounded edges. | **Include.** The change corrects several conspicuous background-image artifacts across supported GroupBox styles. |
| [#14904](https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/pull/14904) | Net11 `RadioButton` with `RightToLeft.Yes` | Adds DPI-scaled glyph padding to the modern RadioButton adapter so the hovered glyph is not clipped at the right-to-left edge. | **Include.** Although small, this is a user-visible RTL and high-DPI correctness fix. |
| [#14887](https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/pull/14887) | `TextBoxBase`; `MaskedTextBox`; `ComboBox`; `NumericUpDown`; `DomainUpDown` | Revises shared Net11 field metrics, non-client TextBox layout, ComboBox child bounds, and UpDown sizing and glyph rendering. The changes reduce oversized single-line controls, prevent descender clipping, align editable ComboBox text, normalize dropdown and button proportions, and correct DPI-dependent geometry. | **Include.** This broad fix changes dimensions and readability for common input controls and auto-sized layouts. |
| [#14865](https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/pull/14865) | `CheckBox.BackColor`; `RadioButton.BackColor` | Makes Net11 CheckBox and RadioButton adapters distinguish the default modern appearance from an explicitly assigned `BackColor`, then use the developer-specified color in layout and painting. | **Include.** It restores expected WinForms property precedence for explicitly configured colors. |
| [#14860](https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/pull/14860) | `Control.VisualStylesMode`; modern `Button` rendering | Preserves an explicit child visual-style override even when it initially matches the parent, preventing a `Classic` child from unexpectedly becoming Net11 after a parent change. It also restricts button accent and background decisions to the modern path for consistent focus rendering. | **Include.** It fixes both visible button focus treatment and the semantics of explicit style overrides. |
| [#14853](https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/pull/14853) | `TextBoxBase`; `ComboBox`; `UpDownBase`; `ModernControlColorMath` | Introduces a shared stable border-color calculation for modern editable controls instead of deriving the border from `ForeColor`. Custom text colors therefore no longer recolor borders, including in dark mode. | **Include.** It restores the expected meaning of `ForeColor` across frequently used editable controls. |
| [#14827](https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/pull/14827) | `ComboBox` with `ComboBoxStyle.Simple` | Corrects modern edit/list region layout, removes conflicting native list borders, preserves the rounded outer frame, adds the intended separator, and fixes clipping and hit testing. This removes unreadable text and unexpected scrollbar or container artifacts. | **Include.** It repairs a materially broken standard ComboBox mode under the new visual style. |
| [#14815](https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/pull/14815) | ToggleSwitch rendering for `CheckBox` and `RadioButton` | Separates switch and text regions, subtracts glyph width and spacing from the text rectangle, and uses bounds-based text drawing. Long RTL text in constrained, non-auto-sized controls can now wrap or clip without overlapping the switch. | **Include.** This is a clear visual and internationalization fix for the new ToggleSwitch appearance. |

Issues.Title: Make MonthCalendar selection tests independent of midnight
Issues.Body:
## Proposed changes

- Use a fixed date and explicitly call `SetDate` before exercising `MinDate`, `MaxDate`, `SelectionStart`, `SelectionEnd`, `SelectionRange`, and `SetSelectionRange`. Theory discovery and control construction no longer need to happen on the same wall-clock day.
- Preserve existing boundary, time-component, repeated-set, event-count, and handle/no-handle assertions. Include the tightly related `SelectionRange` property tests, which delegate to `SetSelectionRange` and have the same assumption.
- Add four deterministic oversized-range cases covering initial selection on the data's day versus the following day, with and without a handle. These exercise both selection-clamping branches without changing the OS clock.

### CI evidence

[Build 1608106, failing MonthCalendar result](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1608106&view=ms.vss-test-web.build-test-results-tab&runId=44442656&resultId=122474&paneView=debug) reported 20 MonthCalendar failures in each of Windows x64 Debug and x86 Debug. The raw xUnit assembly ran from `2026-09-22T23:55:57.7076262+00:00` to `2026-09-23T00:00:07.6202918+00:00`; the linked failing case started at `2026-09-23T00:00:03.4745982+00:00` (the grouped published timestamp is misleading).

Its data described September 22–29 and expected September 23–29, but the new control's default selection was September 23. `SetSelectionRange` therefore trimmed the end instead of advancing the start, yielding actual start September 22. Other affected assertions expected September 22 but observed September 23.

This is an independent test-only PR based on `main`, not stacked on or changing #15180. That PR exposed the failure but its UI input diagnostics are unrelated.

## Customer Impact

No product behavior changes. Removes discovery-to-execution midnight dependence from these unit-test families and reduces spurious CI failures.

## Regression?

Existing test flakiness; no product regression fix.

## Risk

Low: one unit-test source file changes. No product clocks, retries, discovery settings, or public APIs change.

## Test methodology

Arcade targeted Debug builds succeeded with zero warnings/errors:

```powershell
# Process-local environment needed by the existing Framework build helper.
$env:PATH = 'C:\Program Files\Microsoft Visual Studio\18\IntPreview\MSBuild\Current\Bin;' + $env:PATH
$env:MSBuildEnableWorkloadResolver = 'false'
.\build.cmd -projects 'src\test\unit\*Framework\UnsupportedTypes\UnsupportedTypes.csproj' -configuration Debug -verbosity minimal
.\build.cmd -projects src\test\unit\System.Windows.Forms\System.Windows.Forms.Tests.csproj -configuration Debug -verbosity minimal /p:TargetArchitecture=x64
.\build.cmd -projects src\test\unit\System.Windows.Forms\System.Windows.Forms.Tests.csproj -configuration Debug -verbosity minimal /p:TargetArchitecture=x86
```

All **130 targeted cases passed on both confirmed 64-bit and 32-bit hosts**, with zero failures/skips: all 12 consumers of the six modified providers (126 rows) and all four added regression rows. Tests ran through the compiled test entry point using xUnit's exact method filters, not VSTest filtering:

```powershell
$filters = @()
foreach ($property in @('MaxDate', 'MinDate', 'SelectionStart', 'SelectionEnd', 'SelectionRange')) {
    foreach ($operation in @('Set', 'SetWithHandle')) {
        $filters += @('--filter-method', "System.Windows.Forms.Tests.MonthCalendarTests.MonthCalendar_${property}_${operation}_GetReturnsExpected")
    }
}
foreach ($operation in @('Invoke', 'InvokeWithHandle')) {
    $filters += @('--filter-method', "System.Windows.Forms.Tests.MonthCalendarTests.MonthCalendar_SetSelectionRange_${operation}_GetReturnsExpected")
}
$filters += @('--filter-method', 'System.Windows.Forms.Tests.MonthCalendarTests.MonthCalendar_SetSelectionRange_ExceedsMaxSelectionCount_UsesInitialSelection')
$assembly = '.\artifacts\bin\System.Windows.Forms.Tests\Debug\net11.0-windows7.0\System.Windows.Forms.Tests.dll'
& .\.dotnet\dotnet.exe $assembly @filters
& .\.dotnet\x86\dotnet.exe $assembly @filters
```

Also verified the failure mechanism against the actual control: temporarily advancing only `SetSelectionRange_Invoke_GetReturnsExpected`'s initial selection by one day reproduced exactly one failing row (expected January 16, actual January 15; 19/20 passed). Reverted that temporary mutation, rebuilt, and reran all 130 cases successfully on both hosts.

### Limitations and local setup

- Debug targeted tests only; no full solution, Release, or UI integration test runs.
- Nonshown MonthCalendar handles only: no window showing/activation, input injection, or OS clock/registry changes.
- Installed VS MSBuild 18.6 needed process-local `MSBuildEnableWorkloadResolver=false` because the preview SDK's optional workload resolver requires MSBuild 18.7. Repository build configuration and analyzer settings were not changed. The existing `UnsupportedTypes` assembly needed an explicit prerequisite build for this isolated project build.
- Arcade emitted a nonfatal missing-CMake notice; the targeted managed builds completed successfully.

## Test environment(s)

Windows; repository SDK `11.0.100-rc.1.26420.103`; test TFM `net11.0-windows7.0`; repository-installed .NET runtime `12.0.0-alpha.1.26471.108`, x64 and x86. Test class uses the existing `en-US` culture fixture.

Issues.Title: Validate UI test input counts and actual foreground window
Issues.Body:
## Motivation

**This PR adds fail-fast validation and diagnostics to investigate flaky UI tests; it does not make focus acquisition, input delivery, or snapping more reliable.** Today, unsuccessful foreground acquisition or incomplete input insertion can go unnoticed until a later assertion reports only that the form did not snap. The goal is to distinguish those input/setup failures from failures that occur after input was successfully inserted, so a subsequent fix can target an observed cause rather than a guess.

Successful-path behavior is unchanged: the same activation calls and input events are used, and the existing snapping waits remain unchanged. This is more than additional logging, however: if the requested window is not actually foreground, the test now throws **before injecting input**; if Windows inserts fewer events than requested, it throws **after that insertion attempt** instead of continuing with an incomplete sequence. Neither check retries or repairs the failed operation.

The original CI failures did not retain these measurements, so we do not know whether either condition caused them. These checks are an investigative step, not evidence that the flakiness is resolved. If both checks pass and snapping still fails, investigation must continue into subsequent input processing or UI/shell behavior.

## Proposed changes

- Route all six keyboard and seven mouse dispatch sites through one shared `InputSimulator.Send` helper. Require `SendInput` to insert the entire requested batch; otherwise throw with requested/inserted counts and the immediately captured Win32 error. Error 0 is explicitly reported as having no extended error information, not as evidence of UIPI or another cause. The existing generated CsWin32 wrapper clears the native last error and captures it with `Marshal.SetLastPInvokeError`; no new native declaration is needed.
- Correct foreground verification in `SendInput.SendAsync`. Previously, a failed native `SetForegroundWindow` call checked the **requested** window's PID, which normally belongs to the test process regardless of what is actually foreground. Preserve the activation/focus sequence and removal of the temporary topmost flag, then query `GetForegroundWindow` after the `Task.Run` thread switch, immediately before starting the input sequence. Require the requested HWND to be the actual foreground HWND in the test process. On failure report requested/actual HWNDs and PIDs, with PID 0 for a failed lookup. A false activation return does not by itself reject a window that is already foreground.
- Add 15 deterministic regression cases for complete/zero/partial insertion, informative/uninformative error codes, matching/different/null foreground handles, foreign processes, and failed process lookups. Tests use synthetic handles and do not call native input or activation APIs.

## Customer Impact

Test infrastructure only. Missing input or unsuccessful foreground acquisition will fail at the input boundary with actionable diagnostics instead of silently proceeding to downstream UI assertions. No shipping API or product behavior changes.

## Regression?

These are existing validation defects verified on the current base; this PR does not establish when they were introduced or claim they caused a specific CI failure.

Investigation context: [build 1597751](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1597751), associated with #15059, had x86 snapping failures in both [Debug log 66](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/cbb18261-c48f-4abb-8651-8cdcb5474649/_apis/build/builds/1597751/logs/66) and [Release log 70](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/cbb18261-c48f-4abb-8651-8cdcb5474649/_apis/build/builds/1597751/logs/70). No input-count or actual-foreground telemetry was retained. x64 controls passed, and x86 passed on a stage retry, but the retry also changed checkout commit, runtime, and worker, so recovery does not isolate a cause. This is a validation/diagnostic improvement, **not a confirmed flakiness cure**.

## Risk

Limited to UI integration-test infrastructure. The foreground precondition is intentionally stricter: a different window is rejected even if it belongs to the test process. It is a snapshot before the input sequence, not an atomic guarantee against later foreground changes. Count validation checks insertion, not subsequent input processing. No retries, test disabling, registry/OS-policy changes, product changes, or splash-screen changes. Existing 500 ms snapping waits are unchanged.

## Test methodology

- Passed targeted Arcade build: `build.cmd -projects src\test\integration\UIIntegrationTests\System.Windows.Forms.UI.IntegrationTests.csproj -verbosity minimal` (0 warnings, 0 errors).
- Passed all 15 new cases on **x64** using the compiled test executable with `--filter-class System.Windows.Forms.UITests.InputSimulatorTests --filter-class System.Windows.Forms.UITests.SendInputTests --report-trx`.
- Passed the same 15 cases on **x86**, hosting the same AnyCPU test assembly with the repo-local x86 `dotnet.exe` and the same filters.
- Inspected emitted CsWin32 source to verify last-error clearing/capture semantics; `git diff --check` passed.
- **Local limitation:** no global keyboard/mouse synthesis or window activation was performed on this shared workstation. Live UI/snapping behavior remains for PR CI on isolated agents; no local reproduction or end-to-end flakiness claim is made.

## Test environment(s)

Windows build 26200; repository SDK `11.0.100-rc.1.26420.103`; repository runtime `12.0.0-alpha.1.26471.101` (x64 and x86); Debug `net11.0-windows7.0` test assembly.

Issues.Title: Make a ContextMenuStrip opened from the keyboard speak in screen readers
Issues.Body:
Fixes #15178

Related: #3334

## Proposed changes

- `ContextMenuStrip.OnOpened`: raise `UIA_MenuOpenedEventId` also when a UIA client is listening, not only when the accessible object of the menu already exists. The first time a context menu opens that object has never been asked for, so the first opening was silent.
- `ContextMenuStrip.ShowInternal`: when the menu is keyboard activated, select the first item, the same way `ToolStripMenuItem` does for a submenu opened from the keyboard (`SelectNextToolStripItem(start: null, forward: true)`), and the way native Windows menus behave. Nothing had the accessibility focus until an arrow key was pressed. A menu opened with the mouse is not affected.
- `ToolStripItem.Select`: a drop-down without an owner item (a `ContextMenuStrip`) now checks the accessible object of its parent; `OwnerItem?.IsAccessibilityObjectCreated ?? false` was always `false` for it.
- `ToolStripDropDownAccessibleObject.Name`: a `ContextMenuStrip` with no `AccessibleName` and no owner item is named "Context" (new resource `ContextMenuStripDefaultAccessibleName`), like a native context menu, so that screen readers can say "Context menu". On .NET Framework 4.8 this menu did have an accessible name ("DropDown"); on .NET it is empty, so this gives back something that was lost, with a more meaningful value. `AccessibleName` still overrides it, an empty string included.

## Customer Impact

- Screen reader users get no feedback when they open a context menu with Shift+F10 or the Applications key in any WinForms app: they cannot tell whether the menu opened. This is the same report as #3334.

## Regression?

- No.

## Risk

- Low to medium. The visible change is that a context menu opened **from the keyboard** shows its first item selected, as submenus and native menus already do. Menus opened with the mouse, and menus shown by calling `Show` directly, are unchanged.

## Screenshots

### Before

Context menu opened with Shift+F10: no item highlighted.

![Context menu opened from the keyboard, stock .NET 10: no item highlighted](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kastwey/winforms/assets/contextmenustrip-screenshots/screenshots/before-stock-net10.png)

### After

Context menu opened with Shift+F10: the first item, "Open", is highlighted.

![Context menu opened from the keyboard with the change: the first item, Open, is highlighted](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kastwey/winforms/assets/contextmenustrip-screenshots/screenshots/after-patched.png)

## Test methodology

- New unit tests in `ContextMenuStripTests` (keyboard activation selects the first item and skips a separator, mouse activation selects nothing, an empty menu does not throw, the accessible object of a selected item is created when only the menu's existed) and in `ToolStripDropDown_ToolStripDropDownAccessibleObjectTests` (default name, `AccessibleName` wins even when empty, the owner item's name wins while there is one, a plain `ToolStripDropDown` keeps a null name). Five of them fail on `main` without the change.
- `ControlAccessibleObject_GetPropertyValue_Default_Name_ReturnsExpected` keeps a list of the controls that have a default accessible name; `ContextMenuStrip` is added to it.
- Ran the whole `System.Windows.Forms.Tests` suite locally (about 90,130 tests) four times. The first two runs caught the default-name test above, now updated. In the last two, the only failures besides the 10 that also fail on my machine on an unmodified `main` (4 `MdiControlStrip` tests expect "Minimize" and an en-GB Windows says "Minimise", 1 DPI test, 5 `ListBox` tests) were intermittent and unrelated to the change: `AccessibleObject_Navigate_FromForm_OneChild` once (it also fails about one time in three when run alone on the same binaries) and two clipboard tests once, while the clipboard was in use.
- Listened to the UIA and MSAA events of a small app from another process, before and after (logs in the issue).
- Manual testing on Windows 11 with a local build of `release/10.0`:
  - NVDA 2026.2.0: before, silence until an arrow key is pressed; after, "Open, 1 of 4" on opening.
  - JAWS 2026 (2026.2608.25.400) (together with #15177): "Open, 1 of 4" on opening, the arrows read every item, "Leaving menus" on Escape.
  - Narrator: before, "menu" on opening and the items only with the arrows; after, "Open" on opening.

## Accessibility testing

Axe.Windows 2.4.2 (the engine of Accessibility Insights for Windows) run against the repro app, idle and with the context menu of the button open from the keyboard, before and after:

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Idle | 4 errors | 4 errors (the same) |
| Context menu open | 5 errors | 4 errors (the same 4) |

The 4 errors are in the repro app itself, not in WinForms: its button and list are named "Button with a ContextMenuStrip" and "List", which trips `NameExcludesControlType` and `NameExcludesLocalizedControlType`. The error that goes away is `NameNotNull` on the menu ("The Name property of a focusable element must not be null"), the one this PR fixes with the default name. No new error. The `.a11ytest` files can be attached on request.

The change is an accessibility fix. With it, a context menu opened from the keyboard behaves for screen readers exactly like the other WinForms menus on .NET. For comparison, Alt+F on a `MenuStrip` (where WinForms has always selected the first item at once): NVDA and JAWS both say "New, 1 of 3" and neither says "menu". With this change, Shift+F10 on a control gives "Open, 1 of 4" in the same way.

The readers announce the selected item rather than the word "menu" because the focus event of the item follows `MenuOpened` at once. That is how the readers behave with every WinForms menu on .NET (on .NET Framework 4.8 JAWS does announce "File menu" before "New", so this differs between the two frameworks), not something this PR introduces, and I deliberately did not work around it in WinForms (for instance by delaying the selection, or by making the menu claim the keyboard focus while one of its items has it). For NVDA I traced it to its handling of `MenuOpened` for a menu that does not report `HasKeyboardFocus`, and I will report it there.

## Test environment(s)

- .NET SDK 10.0.303, runtime 10.0.11, Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200.

Issues.Title: A ContextMenuStrip opened from the keyboard is silent for screen readers (no MenuOpened the first time, no item focused)
Issues.Body:
## .NET version

.NET 10 (10.0.11). Same code in `main`. The behaviour is also there in .NET 9.

## Did it work in .NET Framework?

No. I built the same repro for .NET Framework 4.8: NVDA 2026.2.0 is silent on opening there too, and no item is selected. (With the arrows it then says "DropDown toolbar, Open", without the position; on .NET the items are read better, "Open, 1 of 4".) The MSAA events on 4.8 are `MENUPOPUPSTART name="DropDown" role=MENUPOPUP` on opening and no `FOCUS` until an arrow key is pressed. So this is a long-standing gap, not a regression.

## Did it work in any of the earlier releases of .NET Core or .NET 5+?

No. #3334 reported it for .NET Core 3.1; it was closed as an NVDA problem after checking that the UIA tree was correct. The tree is correct; the problem is in the events.

## Issue description

Open a `ContextMenuStrip` with Shift+F10 or the Applications key (the menu is just assigned to `Control.ContextMenuStrip`). With NVDA nothing is announced until an arrow key is pressed. I am a blind developer and I hit this in my own app, so I listened to the UIA and MSAA events from another process and read the source. There are three separate causes:

1. **`MenuOpened` is not raised the first time the menu opens.** `ContextMenuStrip.OnOpened` only raises `UIA_MenuOpenedEventId` when `IsAccessibilityObjectCreated` is true. The first time a context menu opens nothing has asked for its accessible object yet: it has no owner item and it was never part of the tree a client walked. From the second opening on, the event is raised.

2. **No item is selected, so nothing gets the accessibility focus.** `ContextMenuStrip.ShowInternal(source, location, isKeyboardActivated)` only turns the mnemonic underlines on. A submenu opened from the keyboard selects its first item (`ToolStripMenuItem` calls `DropDown.SelectNextToolStripItem(start: null, forward: true)`), and so does a native Windows menu opened from the keyboard: for the system menu the WinEvents are `MENUPOPUPSTART` followed at once by `FOCUS` on "Restore".

3. **The focus event of an item can be skipped in a context menu.** `ToolStripItem.Select` decides whether accessibility is on with:

   ```csharp
   IsOnDropDown ? OwnerItem?.IsAccessibilityObjectCreated ?? false : IsParentAccessibilityObjectCreated
   ```

   The items of a `ContextMenuStrip` are on a drop-down that has no `OwnerItem`, so this is always `false` unless the item's own accessible object already exists.

A related point: the menu has no accessible name, because `ToolStripDropDownAccessibleObject.Name` takes it from the owner item and a context menu has none. On .NET Framework 4.8 it was named "DropDown". Native context menus are named "Context", which screen readers announce followed by the role ("Context menu").

<details>
<summary>Measurements: the UIA events seen from another process, before and after</summary>

Stock .NET 10.0.11. First opening with Shift+F10, then Down, Down:

```
(nothing on opening)
FocusChanged: MenuItem "Open"   <- only after pressing Down
FocusChanged: MenuItem "Edit"
MenuClosed:   Menu ""
```

With the proposed changes:

```
MenuOpened:   Menu "Context"
FocusChanged: MenuItem "Open"   <- on opening
FocusChanged: MenuItem "Edit"   <- Down
```

</details>

### What screen readers say with the proposed changes

- NVDA 2026.2.0: "Open, 1 of 4" on opening (it said nothing before).
- JAWS 2026 (2026.2608.25.400): "Open, 1 of 4" on opening, the arrows read every item, and "Leaving menus" on Escape. (This also needs the MSAA regression fix of #15176; without it JAWS reads the items erratically.)
- Narrator: "Open" on opening (before: "menu", and the items only with the arrows).

That is the same experience the readers give with the other WinForms menus on .NET: Alt+F on a `MenuStrip`, where the first item has always been selected at once, gives "New, 1 of 3" in NVDA and in JAWS, and neither says "menu". They announce the focused item rather than the menu because its focus event follows `MenuOpened` at once; that is a matter for the readers (for NVDA I traced it to `MenuOpened` being dropped when the menu does not report `HasKeyboardFocus`, and I will report it there), not something the menu should work around.

## Steps to reproduce

```csharp
Button button = new() { Text = "Button with a ContextMenuStrip", AutoSize = true };
ContextMenuStrip menu = new();
menu.Items.Add("&Open");
menu.Items.Add("&Edit");
button.ContextMenuStrip = menu;
Controls.Add(button);
```

1. Run it with NVDA. Focus the button and press Shift+F10.
2. Nothing is announced. Press Down: "Open, 1 of 2".

I have the changes with unit tests ready and will open a pull request.

A draft pull request with the changes is open alongside this issue, in case it helps to judge the direction; I am happy to adjust it.

Issues.Title: Fix inverted NoClientNotifications check in Control.AccessibilityNotifyClients
Issues.Body:
Fixes #15176

## Proposed changes

- Restore the negation that `Control.AccessibilityNotifyClients(AccessibleEvents, int, int)` had in .NET 9: `NotifyWinEvent` must be called unless the `NoClientNotifications` switch is set, not only when it is set.
- Add unit tests that actually listen to the WinEvent (in-context hook on the test thread). The existing tests only checked that the call did not throw, which is why this went unnoticed.

## Customer Impact

- Since .NET 10, no control raises MSAA WinEvents through `AccessibilityNotifyClients`: menu popup start/end, focus of `ToolStrip` items, and the state, selection, value and name change events. Screen readers and other assistive technologies that rely on MSAA (JAWS among them) get less information from every WinForms app than they did in .NET 9.
- Apps that set `NoClientNotifications` get the opposite of what they asked for: WinEvents are raised only for them.

## Regression?

- Yes, from .NET 9. Introduced by #12840 (620b123): the rename of `LocalAppContextSwitches` to `AppContextSwitches` dropped the `!` on this line only; the other six lines that use the switch kept their expression.

## Risk

- Low. One character; it restores the .NET 9 behaviour, and the switch keeps working as documented.

## Test methodology

- New unit tests in `ControlTests.AccessibilityNotifyClients.cs`: the WinEvent is raised with the right window, object id and 1-based child id; it is not raised when `NoClientNotifications` is set. On `main` without the fix all three fail exactly as the bug predicts (nothing raised by default, raised when the switch is set); with the fix they pass.
- Ran the whole `System.Windows.Forms.Tests` suite locally (90,122 tests), twice with the fix and twice without it. No new failures: the same 10 tests fail on my machine in both cases and are unrelated (4 `MdiControlStrip` tests expect "Minimize" and an en-GB Windows says "Minimise", 1 DPI test, 5 `ListBox` tests). The only tests whose result changes are the three new ones.
- Listened to the WinEvents of a small app from another process (`SetWinEventHook`, out of context) on .NET 9.0.19, on stock .NET 10.0.11 and on a local build of `release/10.0` with the fix: the `OBJID_CLIENT` events with resolvable names are present in .NET 9, absent in .NET 10 and present again with the fix (logs in the issue).
- Manual testing on Windows 11 with a local build of `release/10.0` that contains only this fix, opening a `ContextMenuStrip` with Shift+F10:
  - JAWS 2026 (2026.2608.25.400), before: says "Menu" and nothing else; the arrow keys read nothing for a while, and only after going round the menu a few times do they start reading the items. After: "Context menu, Open" on opening, and the arrows read every item from the first time.
  - JAWS, menu bar (Alt+F on a `MenuStrip`), before: silent the first time. After: "New, 1 of 3".
  - NVDA 2026.2.0: unchanged (it uses UIA for these windows, so it does not depend on the WinEvents).

## Servicing

Could this be considered for servicing in `release/10.0`? It is a regression from .NET 9 in an LTS release, it affects every WinForms app used with an MSAA-based screen reader, and the fix is one character with tests. I first made and tested the fix on `release/10.0` (that is the build the manual testing above was done with), so I can open the backport PR myself if that helps.

## Accessibility testing

This change only restores accessibility events; it does not change any UI.

## Test environment(s)

- .NET SDK 10.0.303, runtime 10.0.11, Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200.

Issues.Title: Regression in .NET 10: controls no longer raise MSAA WinEvents (inverted `NoClientNotifications` check in `Control.AccessibilityNotifyClients`)
Issues.Body:
## .NET version

.NET 10 (10.0.11 runtime, SDK 10.0.303). Still present in `main` (checked at 75072a6) and in `release/10.0` (f8eab87).

## Did it work in .NET Framework?

Yes

## Did it work in any of the earlier releases of .NET Core or .NET 5+?

Yes. It works in .NET 8 and .NET 9 (verified with 9.0.19).

## Issue description

`Control.AccessibilityNotifyClients(AccessibleEvents, int, int)` is the method every control uses to raise MSAA WinEvents (`NotifyWinEvent`). Its guard lost the negation between .NET 9 and .NET 10:

```csharp
// .NET 8
if (IsHandleCreated && AccessibleObject.CanNotifyClients)

// .NET 9
if (IsHandleCreated && !LocalAppContextSwitches.NoClientNotifications)

// .NET 10 and main
if (IsHandleCreated && AppContextSwitches.NoClientNotifications)
```

The negation was dropped in #12840 ("More OLE related refactoring", 620b123), which renamed `LocalAppContextSwitches` to `AppContextSwitches` across 81 files. That PR touched seven lines that use this switch; in the other six the rename kept the expression as it was (four `!AppContextSwitches.NoClientNotifications`, two without negation that had none before). Only this one lost its `!`, so it looks like a slip in a mechanical rename rather than a decision; the PR description does not mention accessibility and there are no review comments.

`NoClientNotifications` means "do not notify accessibility clients" and is `false` by default, so since .NET 10 `NotifyWinEvent` is only called when the application has asked for **no** notifications, that is, never by default. Every other use of the switch in the code base is negated (`AccessibleObject.cs`, `Control.ControlAccessibleObject.cs`, `MessageBox.cs`).

The result is that assistive technologies that rely on MSAA WinEvents stop receiving everything raised through this method: `SystemMenuPopupStart`/`SystemMenuPopupEnd` of a `ContextMenuStrip`, `SystemMenuStart`/`SystemMenuEnd` of a `MenuStrip`, the `Focus` event of `ToolStrip` items, and the state, selection, value and name change events raised by the controls.

I am a blind developer and I found this while investigating why JAWS and NVDA behave differently with a WinForms app after moving it to .NET 10. What a JAWS 2026 user gets today when opening a `ContextMenuStrip` with Shift+F10: "Menu" and nothing else; the arrow keys read nothing for a while, and only after going round the menu a few times do they start reading the items. The menu bar is affected too: the first Alt+F is silent. With the one-character fix applied to a local build of `release/10.0`, JAWS says "Context menu, Open" on opening and the arrows read every item from the first time; Alt+F says "New, 1 of 3". NVDA is not affected because it uses UIA for these windows.

<details>
<summary>Measurements: the WinEvents seen from another process on .NET Framework 4.8, .NET 9, .NET 10 and .NET 10 with the fix</summary>

I listened to the WinEvents of the repro app below from another process (`SetWinEventHook`, out of context) while opening a context menu with Shift+F10 and pressing Down twice. For every event I called `AccessibleObjectFromEvent`.

.NET Framework 4.8 raises the same events (`MENUPOPUPSTART idObject=-4 name="DropDown" role=MENUPOPUP`, then `FOCUS idObject=-4 idChild=1 name="Open" role=MENUITEM`...), so .NET 10 is the first version in which they are missing.

.NET 9.0.19, stock — real MSAA events, resolvable:

```
MENUPOPUPSTART idObject=-4 idChild=0 name=""     role=MENUPOPUP
FOCUS          idObject=-4 idChild=1 name="Open" role=MENUITEM
FOCUS          idObject=-4 idChild=2 name="Edit" role=MENUITEM
```

.NET 10.0.11, stock — none of them. The only WinEvents left are the ones Windows bridges from the UIA events, which carry a positive `idObject` and cannot be resolved (`AccessibleObjectFromEvent` returns `E_FAIL`):

```
FOCUS          idObject=1 idChild=0  (AccessibleObjectFromEvent hr=0x80004005)
FOCUS          idObject=2 idChild=0  (AccessibleObjectFromEvent hr=0x80004005)
```

.NET 10 with the fix — back to the .NET 9 behaviour:

```
MENUPOPUPSTART idObject=-4 idChild=0 role=MENUPOPUP
FOCUS          idObject=-4 idChild=1 name="Open" role=MENUITEM
FOCUS          idObject=-4 idChild=2 name="Edit" role=MENUITEM
```

</details>

The existing unit tests of `AccessibilityNotifyClients` only check that the call does not throw, which is why the regression went unnoticed.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create a WinForms app targeting `net10.0-windows` with this in the form:

   ```csharp
   Button button = new() { Text = "Button with a ContextMenuStrip", AutoSize = true };
   ContextMenuStrip menu = new();
   menu.Items.Add("&Open");
   menu.Items.Add("&Edit");
   button.ContextMenuStrip = menu;
   Controls.Add(button);
   ```
2. From another process, install a WinEvent hook for the app (or use Accessible Event Watcher / AccEvent from the Windows SDK, in WinEvents mode).
3. Focus the button, press Shift+F10, then Down.
4. No `EVENT_SYSTEM_MENUPOPUPSTART` and no `EVENT_OBJECT_FOCUS` with `idObject = OBJID_CLIENT` arrive. The same app targeting `net9.0-windows` raises them.

I have a fix with unit tests ready and will open a pull request.

However, the screen reader announces only the option name and does not convey its selected state.
